newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia central bank widens intervention band.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia central bank widens intervention band.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank said on Wednesday it will widen its intervention band to eight percent from five percent effective immediately.
It said also in a statement that the minimum reserve requirement ratio of banks will be raised to five percent from three percent effective from April 16, 1997.

The central bank said in a statement obtained by Reuters the move was in line with the policy to contain the overheating economy, to reduce speculative trading in financial markets and to strengthen the ability of the bank to control currency fluctuations.
The central bank is scheduled to announce the new intervention band at around 0800 GMT.
The intervention band allows the bank to intervene in the foreign exchange market when market rates move out of the band that the bank fixes on a daily basis.
Bank Indonesia widened its intervention band last in June this year to five percent from three percent.
The central bank's intervention rate on Tuesday was at 2,344.0/2,462.0.
